transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, but... I came in because I've been struggling a bit at work lately. 

I'm a production manager, and usually, I try to be a really dedicated employee. Like, recently I was launching all these nonstop plant redesign projects, and I was calling our suppliers after hours just to get ahead, and I even rewrote the whole shift plan entirely by myself. I really just wanted to do a great job for the company and make sure everything was running smoothly, you know? 

But... um... lately, I've just suddenly found myself completely unable to keep up with the very plans I had just set in motion. It's actually really embarrassing to admit that I'm dropping the ball now after taking on so much. I feel terrible about it. I just want to get back to being a good, reliable manager. Is... is that the kind of thing you can help me with?
Have you been worrying excessively about things beyond just your work performance?

Um, no... I don't think so. I mean, I hope I'm understanding you right, but I don't really worry about other things excessively. I try to be a pretty positive person, usually. 

It's really just the work stuff right now, mostly because I just hate feeling like I'm letting my team down. I just want to be reliable for them. But outside of the plant, I don't really sit around stressing about other parts of my life. I try to keep everything else pretty manageable. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

Um, well... I guess I have been feeling a little down. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or anything, because I know I have a lot to be thankful for. But... lately, I wake up in my temporary apartment and there's just this... this heavy, hollow feeling. 

It's like... it's like the day is already ruined before I even drive to the plant, if that makes sense. I try really hard to shake it off, I really do, because I know I need to be upbeat for the team. But it's just been lingering there. Is that... is that normal for someone going through a rough patch at work? I hope I'm not overreacting by feeling this way.
Have you been enjoying activities that you usually find pleasurable?

Um, well... I guess I still try to enjoy things, you know? I mean, I really don't want to sound ungrateful or like I'm just giving up on everything. 

Normally, I love hiking on the weekends, or even just trying out new recipes. But lately... um, I don't know if I'm just tired from everything at work, but I haven't really had the energy to do those things. Like, I'll think about going for a walk, but then I just kind of sit on the couch instead. I mean, I still *want* to like those things, I just... haven't been doing them as much. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy. I really do try to stay active when I can. Is it okay that I'm just feeling a little too worn out for my hobbies right now?
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like rapid heartbeat, sweating, or trembling lately?

Um, no... I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, my heart feels fine, and I definitely haven't been trembling or anything. I guess if I'm walking the production floor at the plant it gets a little warm, but... not like a nervous sweat, you know? 

I really hope it's a good thing that I don't have those physical issues. I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. Does that... does that answer your question okay?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um, well... I guess it's been a little while now. I really hope it doesn't seem like I've just been letting things slide, but... it's been about three months. 

This heavy stretch just kind of settled in, and I really tried to just push through it on my own at first. I promise I did. But then with the move to the temporary apartment, and taking on this new assignment at the plant... it's just made it a lot harder to manage everything. I didn't want to make a fuss because I know everyone gets stressed with relocations and new roles, you know? 

Do you think three months is... I mean, is it okay that it's taking me this long to adjust? I really am trying my best to get back on track, I just want to make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing.
Are there things that you used to enjoy doing, but now don't find pleasure in?

Um, well... I guess I kind of mentioned the hiking and the cooking earlier. I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm answering you right. 

I don't think there's really anything else, though. I mean, I still try to keep up with my friends when I can, and I still read a little bit before bed. It's just... maybe I'm just a little too tired for the bigger hobbies right now, but I haven't completely stopped liking things, I promise. 

Is that... does that make sense? I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing absolutely nothing all the time. I'm still trying, you know?
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicide recently?

Oh! Um, no. No, definitely not. I really hope I didn't say something earlier to make you worry about that. I promise I haven't had any thoughts like that at all. 

I mean, things have been heavy lately, sure, but I would never... I'm really trying my best to handle everything, and I definitely want to be here to get it all sorted out. I hope that's a relief to hear? I just really want to reassure you that I'm safe, and I'm totally willing to do whatever we need to do to get me feeling better. Is it okay that I'm just dealing with the tiredness and the mood stuff, and not... you know, the scarier things?
Have you experienced a significant loss of interest in activities you once enjoyed most of the day?

Um, well... I know you just asked about the things I used to enjoy, and I really hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression here. I mean, I'm not just lying in bed staring at the wall all day or anything like that. I promise I'm still getting up and going to the plant and doing my job. 

It's just... I guess the things I mentioned before, the hiking and the cooking, it's not like I've lost interest in them completely. It's more that I just haven't had the energy for them most of the day, you know? Like, I'll think about trying a new recipe, but then I just feel so drained from work and the move that I end up ordering takeout instead. 

But I'm still trying to stay engaged, I really am. I don't want you to think I've just given up on everything. Is it... is it normal to just feel a little disconnected from things when you're this tired? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on.
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty most of the time lately?

Um, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I really hope I'm not coming across as someone who just sits around feeling sorry for myself. I definitely don't feel worthless. I know I'm good at my job at the plant, and I try really hard to be a good person and do the right things. 

Sometimes I guess I feel a little bad that I'm not doing as much as I usually do, like with the cooking or seeing my friends, but I wouldn't call it... guilt, exactly? Just, you know, wishing I had a bit more energy to be my normal self. I try to remind myself that it's just a phase and I'm doing my best. I really hope that's the right way to look at it? I just want to make sure I'm handling this the way I'm supposed to.
Have you been experiencing a depressed mood for most of the day?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I'm, like, completely miserable or anything. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining too much. I know I have a good job and things to be grateful for. 

But, I guess... lately, I do wake up in the temporary apartment with this... this heavy, sort of hollow feeling? It's almost like the day feels a bit ruined before I even drive to the plant. I try really hard to shake it off, though! I always make sure I get dressed and go to work, and I put on a good face for everyone there. 

I just... I hope it's okay to admit that it's been a little hard to feel upbeat most of the day. I really am trying to stay positive, though. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information without sounding like I'm not trying my best.
Have you been experiencing a lack of interest in social activities?

Um, well... no, not really. I mean, I definitely haven't just stopped caring about my friends or anything like that! I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm isolating myself. I know how important it is to keep up with people.

I guess with the move and everything at the plant, I haven't been going out *quite* as much as I used to, but I still text my friends and try to keep in touch. It's just that by the time the weekend rolls around, I'm usually pretty tired, so maybe I'll suggest a quiet night in instead of going out to a loud bar or something. 

But I'm still social, I promise! I just... maybe I need a little more downtime right now? I hope that's an okay way to handle things when you're feeling a bit drained. Is it normal to just want things to be a little more low-key for a while? I just want to make sure I'm not doing anything wrong by taking it easy.
Have you been experiencing a depressed mood nearly every day?

Um, I wouldn't say *every* single day. I really don't want you to think I'm just miserable all the time, because I'm definitely not! I mean, I have days where I feel totally fine, especially if things go well at the plant or if I get a good night's sleep. 

I guess it's just... it's been more days than not lately where I have that heavy feeling I mentioned? But I really try not to let it take over the whole week. Like, if I have a bad Tuesday, I make sure I push myself extra hard on Wednesday to have a good day. 

So, no, not every day. Just... maybe a bit more often than I'd like right now. But I'm really working on it, I promise. Does that sound like I'm managing it okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture without making it sound worse than it is.
For how long have you been waking up with that heavy, hollow feeling?

Um, well... I guess it's been a little while now. I really hope it doesn't sound like I've just been letting things slide, because I really have been trying to push through it. 

I'd say... maybe around three months? Give or take? It kind of started around the time I had to move into the temporary apartment and take on this new assignment at the plant. I think all the changes just made it a bit trickier to manage, you know? I really don't want to blame my job, because I'm so grateful for the opportunity, but the transition has just been... a lot. 

So, yeah, about three months of that heavy stretch. But I'm still showing up every day! I'm really trying my best to handle it all. Is it pretty normal for a big move and a new role to throw you off for a few months like that? I just hope I'm not overreacting to normal stress.
Have you been experiencing significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns lately?

Um, well... I guess things have been a little bit uneven lately? But I really try to make sure I'm still getting enough nutrition, I promise! I definitely don't want you to think I'm neglecting myself. 

My eating has just been... kind of all over the place, I suppose. With the new schedule at the plant, sometimes I get so caught up in making sure everything is running smoothly that I'll look at the clock and it's 4 p.m. and all I've had is coffee. But I always make up for it! It's just... some nights I get back to the apartment and I end up just standing in the kitchen eating takeout straight from the container, even when I'm not actually that hungry. 

I know that's probably not the best habit, and I'm really going to try to start meal-prepping on Sundays so I have proper dinners. That's a good plan, right? I just hope it doesn't sound like I'm totally out of control or anything. Is it normal for your appetite to get a little scrambled when you're dealing with a lot of changes at work?
Have you been experiencing a lack of energy or fatigue nearly every day?

Um, energy... well, I wouldn't say I'm fatigued every single day. I really want to make sure I'm being clear that I'm still getting my job done! I'm definitely not just lying in bed all day or anything like that. 

I mean, sure, I get tired, but who doesn't, right? Especially with the new plant assignment. It's a lot of running around the floor and managing the different lines. So it makes sense that I'd be a little drained by the time I get back to the apartment. 

But I push through it! I always make sure I'm up and ready for my shift. I might need an extra cup of coffee some afternoons, but I'm really trying my best not to let it affect my performance. I just... I don't want you to think I'm slacking off or anything. It's totally normal to feel a bit worn out when you're taking on more responsibility at work, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm not making a big deal out of normal tiredness.
Have you been experiencing a lack of interest in most activities most of the day?

Um... interest in things? I guess I'm still doing most of what I normally do. I really try to keep busy, you know? I don't want to just sit around and do nothing. 

I mean, I still go to work every day, and I'm still managing the lines at the plant, so I'm definitely staying active! I guess maybe when I get home to the apartment, I don't always feel like... doing much else? I used to read a bit more, or maybe watch a show, and lately I just kind of sit there for a while. But I think that's just because I'm giving so much at work, right? 

I really don't want it to sound like I've stopped caring about things. I still care! It's just... maybe my focus is just entirely on the job right now. That's a good thing, right? Being dedicated to your work? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by prioritizing my responsibilities. It's pretty normal to not have a ton of hobbies when you're focusing on a big career transition, isn't it?
Have you been feeling hopeless most of the time lately?

Um, hopeless? I... I really don't want to sound dramatic, and I definitely haven't given up or anything! I always try to keep a good attitude, I promise. 

It's just... well, I guess lately, when I wake up in the temporary apartment, I've been getting this... this really heavy, hollow feeling? It's kind of hard to explain. It almost feels like the day is already ruined before I even drive to the plant. 

But I still go! I always make sure I get in the car and do my job. I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself or being a negative person. It's probably just a normal funk, right? Lots of people wake up feeling a little down when they're dealing with a lot of stress and a new environment, don't they? I'm really trying my best to stay positive about it all, I really am.
Do you feel that your depressive symptoms are interfering with your daily life most of the time?

Um, interfering? I... I really try my absolute hardest not to let that happen. I always want to pull my weight at the plant, I promise! But... I guess... maybe just a little bit lately? 

I'm honestly so embarrassed to even say this, because I really don't want you to think I'm incapable or that I can't handle my responsibilities. But... well, there was this one incident recently. I actually had to ask to be pulled out of a shift-planning meeting. I just... I sort of froze up, and I wasn't able to carry out the basic production decisions that my role really depends on. 

And, um... occupational health ended up getting involved. 

I felt so terrible about it, I really did. I didn't want to make a fuss or cause any trouble for the team. I'm usually so good at my job! It's just... it's normal to get a little overwhelmed and need to step away for a minute when you're managing so much, isn't it? I just really hope everyone knows I'm still completely dedicated to the work.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long I have been experiencing the depressed mood (the heavy, hollow feeling), which corresponds to the depressive episode duration.

patient.answer:
Um, well... I guess it's been a little while now. I really hope it doesn't sound like I've just been letting things slide, because I really have been trying to push through it. 

I'd say... maybe around three months? Give or take? It kind of started around the time I had to move into the temporary apartment and take on this new assignment at the plant. I think all the changes just made it a bit trickier to manage, you know? I really don't want to blame my job, because I'm so grateful for the opportunity, but the transition has just been... a lot. 

So, yeah, about three months of that heavy stretch. But I'm still showing up every day! I'm really trying my best to handle it all. Is it pretty normal for a big move and a new role to throw you off for a few months like that? I just hope I'm not overreacting to normal stress.

doctor.question: Have you been experiencing significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns lately?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about changes in appetite and sleep. I am selecting the symptom related to appetite changes to address the first part of the question.

patient.answer:
Um, well... I guess things have been a little bit uneven lately? But I really try to make sure I'm still getting enough nutrition, I promise! I definitely don't want you to think I'm neglecting myself. 

My eating has just been... kind of all over the place, I suppose. With the new schedule at the plant, sometimes I get so caught up in making sure everything is running smoothly that I'll look at the clock and it's 4 p.m. and all I've had is coffee. But I always make up for it! It's just... some nights I get back to the apartment and I end up just standing in the kitchen eating takeout straight from the container, even when I'm not actually that hungry. 

I know that's probably not the best habit, and I'm really going to try to start meal-prepping on Sundays so I have proper dinners. That's a good plan, right? I just hope it doesn't sound like I'm totally out of control or anything. Is it normal for your appetite to get a little scrambled when you're dealing with a lot of changes at work?

doctor.question: Have you been experiencing a lack of energy or fatigue nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about fatigue or loss of energy (typically S029), which is not included in the patient's symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Um, energy... well, I wouldn't say I'm fatigued every single day. I really want to make sure I'm being clear that I'm still getting my job done! I'm definitely not just lying in bed all day or anything like that. 

I mean, sure, I get tired, but who doesn't, right? Especially with the new plant assignment. It's a lot of running around the floor and managing the different lines. So it makes sense that I'd be a little drained by the time I get back to the apartment. 

But I push through it! I always make sure I'm up and ready for my shift. I might need an extra cup of coffee some afternoons, but I'm really trying my best not to let it affect my performance. I just... I don't want you to think I'm slacking off or anything. It's totally normal to feel a bit worn out when you're taking on more responsibility at work, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm not making a big deal out of normal tiredness.

doctor.intent: Determine the severity of the patient's depressive symptoms to differentiate between mild and moderate depressive episodes
doctor.question: Have you been experiencing a lack of interest in most activities most of the day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a lack of interest or pleasure in activities (anhedonia), which is not listed in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Um... interest in things? I guess I'm still doing most of what I normally do. I really try to keep busy, you know? I don't want to just sit around and do nothing. 

I mean, I still go to work every day, and I'm still managing the lines at the plant, so I'm definitely staying active! I guess maybe when I get home to the apartment, I don't always feel like... doing much else? I used to read a bit more, or maybe watch a show, and lately I just kind of sit there for a while. But I think that's just because I'm giving so much at work, right? 

I really don't want it to sound like I've stopped caring about things. I still care! It's just... maybe my focus is just entirely on the job right now. That's a good thing, right? Being dedicated to your work? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by prioritizing my responsibilities. It's pretty normal to not have a ton of hobbies when you're focusing on a big career transition, isn't it?

patient.answer:
Um, hopeless? I... I really don't want to sound dramatic, and I definitely haven't given up or anything! I always try to keep a good attitude, I promise. 

It's just... well, I guess lately, when I wake up in the temporary apartment, I've been getting this... this really heavy, hollow feeling? It's kind of hard to explain. It almost feels like the day is already ruined before I even drive to the plant. 

But I still go! I always make sure I get in the car and do my job. I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself or being a negative person. It's probably just a normal funk, right? Lots of people wake up feeling a little down when they're dealing with a lot of stress and a new environment, don't they? I'm really trying my best to stay positive about it all, I really am.

target_item.reason: The doctor's question asks if the depressive symptoms are interfering with daily life, which corresponds directly to functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Um, interfering? I... I really try my absolute hardest not to let that happen. I always want to pull my weight at the plant, I promise! But... I guess... maybe just a little bit lately? 

I'm honestly so embarrassed to even say this, because I really don't want you to think I'm incapable or that I can't handle my responsibilities. But... well, there was this one incident recently. I actually had to ask to be pulled out of a shift-planning meeting. I just... I sort of froze up, and I wasn't able to carry out the basic production decisions that my role really depends on. 

And, um... occupational health ended up getting involved. 

I felt so terrible about it, I really did. I didn't want to make a fuss or cause any trouble for the team. I'm usually so good at my job! It's just... it's normal to get a little overwhelmed and need to step away for a minute when you're managing so much, isn't it? I just really hope everyone knows I'm still completely dedicated to the work.
